 Darryn Peterson filled up the stat sheet with 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, two steals, three blocks, and three 3-pointers on Friday. 
 Peterson got more aggressive in the second half, and the offense started to get going again in the second half because of him. This is the type of game that people were hoping for when the Jazz drafted him 2 nd overall in last year’s draft. He looked more confident and got to the line for six free throws. Granted, four of them were because the Jazz were in the bonus, but its still good to see the defensive stats in this game. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Keyonte George (ankle) will not return to Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 George sprained his right ankle early in the third quarter and has since returned to the locker room. With their starting point guard done for the night, the Jazz will rely more on Isaiah Collier and Darryn Peterson.

 Keyonte George (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 George is now questionable after not appearing on Utah’s initial injury report. If he can’t play, Isaiah Collier and Darryn Peterson stand to gain the most in playmaking responsibilities. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson had 7 points (2-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, and seven assists on Wednesday against the Pelicans. 
 While this wasn’t an amazing game from Darryn Peterson, he is getting prioritized more. The main difference now is that he’s now running as the backup point guard instead of Isaiah Collier which has really helped Darryn’s assist numbers. This is great for Darryn in dynasty if you have him, because that is the skill that he needs to work on for him to develop into a high-level fantasy player. In redraft leagues, he’s worth a stream if you’re looking for points and some assists, but not more than that. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Darry Peterson recorded 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Peterson has scored in double figures in each of Utah’s last three games. Against the Trail Blazers, he wasn’t at his best, committing three turnovers, but the rookie guard still finished with a full stat line. Peterson played the entire fourth quarter, sharing the court with Keyonte George (8/3/4/1) for seven minutes and Isaiah Collier (8/1/4/2) for the other five. According to Cleaning the Glass, Peterson has played 90% of his minutes at shooting guard thus far. That split appears unlikely to change anytime soon, which may lower his fantasy ceiling.

 Darryn Peterson put up 18 points (4-of-13 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in an overtime loss to the Spurs. 
 Obviously you want Darryn to be more efficient from the field, but he got his shot attempts up which is what you want to see. He did leave the game in the first quarter with a head injury but returned. He did not close the game which is notable. He will continue to get better, and this is a good game all things considered, but the fantasy upside for this season isn’t very high.

 Guard 
 #22 
 Darryn Peterson puts up 9 points (3-of-7 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, and three assists in NBA debut. 
 It was a difficult night all around for the Jazz. Obviously, we would want him to be more aggressive, but it was his first real NBA game. He’ll be much better than this. I like the fact that he was second on the team in minutes, which shows the trust Will Hardy has in him. If you have him, be patient, but he was going later in redraft leagues anyway, so if he doesn’t start producing soon, you can feel free to move on. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 Darryn Peterson finished Monday’s exhibition against the Spurs with 14 points (5-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 Peterson was the lone Jazz starter to see any action after halftime, logging nine minutes in the third quarter. The Jazz inserted Isaiah Collier (11 points, three rebounds, six assists, five steals, and one three-pointer) to start the second half, suggesting they currently view Peterson solely as a two-guard. His taking that role when he’s on the floor with Keyonte George isn’t a surprise, but Peterson may not get many point guard minutes when Utah’s PG1 sits. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 Darryn Peterson went 1-of-5 and finished with three points in Sunday’s preseason win over the Nuggets. 
 Peterson also missed both of his three-point attempts. Though it was a poor effort offensively, Peterson was solid on the defensive end with six boards and a steal, and he chipped in two dimes to round out his final stat line. Better days are ahead for the No. 2 pick, and fantasy managers don’t need to read much into this performance. 
 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 Darryn Peterson led the Jazz with 24 points (6-of-18 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one block, two three-pointers and eight turnovers in a 92-88 loss to the Wizards on Thursday. 
 Peterson was a star during summer league in Salt Lake City, and that commanded the attention of Washington’s defense for the entire game. From the beginning, the Wizards applied full-court pressure when Peterson brought the ball up and made his life incredibly difficult. Though he still had some star flashes, this was by far his worst performance of the summer. He was reckless with the ball at times and committed nine fouls. He’ll look to bounce back against the Clippers on Sunday.

 Austin Reaves exploded for a season-high 43 points (14-of-27 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), five rebounds and four assists over 37 minutes to power the Lakers to a 121-116 win over the Pistons on Sunday.
 No Luka Dončić, no problem. Reaves picked up the slack from a creation standpoint with the current MVP frontrunner sidelined by a back issue in this one. Dončić entered the contest averaging a league-best 40.1 points per game, leaving a significant void for the Lakers to fill. It wasn’t an issue for Reaves, who embraced the expanded offensive responsibilities, repeatedly getting to his spots and making Detroit pay in one-on-one situations from the mid-range. He poured in a team-high 19 first-half points to give Los Angeles a 13-point advantage at the break before tacking on 12 more in the third quarter alone. He drilled a crowd-silencing stepback three-pointer to give Los Angeles an eight-point lead in the final minute. It’s abundantly clear that his fantasy appeal rises exponentially whenever Dončić is out of the lineup. The Lakers continue their current road trip with a three-game week that includes showdowns against the Hawks, Bucks and Suns.
 -  George Bissell

 Daniss Jenkins tallied a career-high 31 points (9-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists and one steal over 32 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Jenkins erupted for a game-high 22 first-half points, shooting 7-of-9 from the floor and 6-of-7 from three-point range in just 13 minutes off the bench. He capped the spectacular half by burying his sixth triple just over one second before the buzzer, sending the crowd into halftime with one final highlight. His sublime effort provided a much-needed lift for Detroit on an off-night for Cade Cunningham, who was held to just - points. The 25-year-old backup point guard knocked down 8-of-14 from three-point range, eclipsing the 20-point threshold for the first time this season. He doesn’t offer a ton of fantasy appeal in a bench role, but that could change if he continues to shoot over 40 percent from downtown. The Pistons have a three-game week on tap that features a pair of matchups against the lowly Wizards before a road tilt against the Heat.
 -  George Bissell

 Walker Kessler recorded a double-double with 12 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 16 rebounds, four assists, one steal and three blocks over 29 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Pistons.
 The 16 boards were a season-high for Kessler as he recorded his fifth double-digit rebounding performance of his Lakers debut, taking advantage of the absence of Detroit’s powerful center Jalen Duren, who remains out with a hamstring injury. He’s notched all five of those efforts over his last six games since October 30. He came up with a key offensive rebound and converted a three-point play to give the Lakers a commanding eight-point advantage with just over two minutes left in regulation. The Lakers have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Hawks, Bucks and Suns.

 Kevin Huerter went off for 24 points (9-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, two steals and five blocks over 35 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Huerter provided a significant spark off Detroit’s bench, helping the Pistons claw back from a nearly 30-point deficit with 10 points in the third quarter. His most impressive moment of the period, however, came as a facilitator rather than a scorer, as he threaded a nifty no-look, over-the-shoulder pass to teammate Daniss Jenkins for a corner three. He also posted an unexpected five blocks as well. His sublime all-around effort helped make up for an off-night for franchise building block Cade Cunningham, who was held scoreless in the first half and finished with just 14 points. The Pistons have a three-game week on tap that features a pair of matchups against the lowly Wizards before a road tilt against the Heat.
